data.title: Why Rivers Flood
data.passage: Heavy spring rains fall on the mountains, so melting snow fills the riverbeds. This fast rushing water overflows the banks because the soil is already soaked with water. As a result, muddy water spreads across nearby farms. People build tall walls of sandbags to protect their homes. Therefore, communities stay safe during heavy storms.
